questions.problem: What is the quotient of ${x}^{4}-3{x}^{2}-4$ divided by ${x}^{2}+1?$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{3}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
{x}^{4}-3{x}^{2}-4={x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+0x-4
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}-4 \\  & {x}^{2}+1\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+0x-4\,\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{4}+0{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,-4{x}^{2}+0x-4 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,4{x}^{2}+0x-4}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is ${x}^{2}-4,$ and

- the remainder is $0.$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing Polynomials When the Dividend Contains Zero Coefficients
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the $x$ term. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing term with a zero coefficient, as follows:

$$
2{x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+1\,=\,2{x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+0x+1
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,2x+1 \\  & {x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+x-4\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,2{x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+0x+1\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{2{x}^{4}-4{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-8x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+8x+1 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+x-4}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,3{x}^{2}+7x+5\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, 

- the quotient is $2x+1,$ and

- the remainder is $3{x}^{2}+7x+5.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2{x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}+1}{\,{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+x-4\,} & =2x+1+\frac{3{x}^{2}+7x+5}{{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+x-4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Express $\frac{-9{x}^{3}+22x}{\,-3x+4\,}$ in the form $q(x)+\frac{r(x)}{\,-3x+4\,},$ where $q(x)$ is the quotient and $r(x)$ is the reminder of the division.$$

| $-9{x}^{3}+22x$ | __ | {{field-1}} | $+$ | {{field-2}} |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-3x+4$ | __ |  |  | $-3x+4$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{2}$ term and the constant term. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
-9{x}^{3}+22x\,=\,-9{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+22x+0
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,3{x}^{2}+4x-2 \\  & -3x+4\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,-9{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+22x+0\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,{-9{x}^{3}+12{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,-12{x}^{2}+22x+0 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,{-\,12{x}^{2}+16x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,6x+0 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\,6x-8}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,8\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, 

- the quotient is $3{x}^{2}+4x-2,$ and

- the remainder is $8.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-9{x}^{3}+22x}{\,-3x+4\,} & =3{x}^{2}+4x-2+\frac{8}{-3x+4}.\end{aligned}
$$
